summary: All three available evidence blocks point the same way: the region ensemble is LTE 0.8202726542949677 vs DVB-T 0.17874850740190595 vs WiFi 0.0009788264530167605 (top1-top2 margin 0.6415241468930617, normalized entropy 0.4342372794199599, the most concentrated ensemble in this series), two of three members independently place LTE at ~0.9986 with window agreement 1.0, and the 64 global IQ features describe a stationary, continuous, wideband, near-Gaussian multi-carrier emission with no burst gaps and no dominant single-carrier or strong quadratic-coupling structure. The periodicity stage is below its frozen reliability margin (margin 0.015417195856571198 < 0.021475793793797496) with all candidate correlations at 0.034-0.050, i.e. insufficient periodicity evidence only; reliable=false is not evidence that DVB-T is true and is not a counter-argument against LTE, so it neither corroborates nor overturns the ensemble. Recommendation is the only member-dissenting class is a near tie (DVB-T 0.5340903997421265 vs LTE 0.4632702171802521 in iq_member_3) whose contribution is an in-region window flip, not a stable class proposal, hence medium rather than higher confidence.
model_evidence: Ensemble (mean_probability_across_members): LTE 0.8202726542949677, DVB-T 0.17874850740190595, WiFi 0.0009788264530167605; top1 LTE with margin 0.6415241468930617 and normalized_entropy 0.4342372794199599.

iq_member_3: region top1 DVB-T 0.5340903997421265 vs LTE 0.4632702171802521 (WiFi 0.002639354672282934) — a near tie, not a confident dissent; window_agreement ratio 0.5, windows LTE 0.7306716442108154 then DVB-T 0.8001691102981567.

risk_gate: unanimous_member_region_top1 = false, unique_top1_labels = [LTE, DVB-T], reason = member_region_top1_disagreement, so the single dissenting member is recorded as conflict rather than smoothed away.

Window-level direction: window 0 is LTE for all three members (0.9975759387016296, 0.9981092214584351, 0.7306716442108154) and window 1 is LTE for two members (0.999632716178894, 0.9997777342796326) while iq_member_3 flips to DVB-T 0.8001691102981567, so the region label rests on two members that are stationary across both windows at near-certainty.
WiFi is effectively excluded by the model evidence: no member places WiFi above 0.002639354672282934 and the ensemble gives it 0.0009788264530167605.
periodicity_evidence: Energy-normalized complex autocorrelation over the complete continuous region (sample_rate 1000000.0 Hz, 4096 samples): period_66p67us lag 67 correlation 0.03416508436203003 (lte_score), period_224us lag 223 correlation 0.04958228021860123 (dvbt_2k_score), period_896us lag 897 correlation 0.041859567165374756 (dvbt_8k_score); scores prediction_label DVB-T with margin 0.015417195856571198.
Frozen gate: reliability_margin 0.021475793793797496, eligible = true, reliable = false, resolved = false, changed = false; review_reason = periodicity_below_threshold.

The nominal periodicity margin 0.015417195856571198 is below the frozen reliability_margin 0.021475793793797496, and all three candidate correlations (0.03416508436203003, 0.04958228021860123, 0.041859567165374756) are of the same low order as the noise-level correlations seen elsewhere in this series, so no candidate period is established.
reliable=false means insufficient periodicity evidence only: it does not establish DVB-T, does not contradict LTE, and cannot be used as a counter-argument against the ensemble.

eligible=true means the gate was in scope for this case (member top1 labels are LTE/DVB-T only, no WiFi), so its DVB-T-leaning prediction_label is a within-scope but unresolved signal; because resolved=false and changed=false, it produced no label change and carries no admissible class support.
Automatic resolution remained unresolved, so the review question is left to the ensemble and feature evidence rather than being settled by the gate.
feature_evidence: Global feature block present: feature_schema_id matlab_iq_features_64_v2, extraction_scope complete_continuous_region, extraction_count 1, preprocessing remove_dc = true and rms_normalize = true, feature_count 64. These are statistical descriptors of this one region, not class labels or protocol detections.

Amplitude/order statistics: time_rms_amplitude 1.0 (RMS-normalized, so a quality-control value per the reference), time_papr_db 9.463398933410645 (elevated, compatible with a multi-carrier emission but also producible by impulsive outliers, not decisive alone), time_amplitude_skewness 0.7112759947776794 and time_envelope_cv 0.5362773537635803 (mild envelope asymmetry and moderate envelope fluctuation), time_amplitude_entropy 0.7994745969772339 (broad amplitude-distribution dispersion).

Envelope kurtosis: time_amplitude_kurtosis 3.354395866394043 (plain kurtosis, no -3 offset in the implementation) is close to the Gaussian reference of 3, i.e. no pronounced spiky or heavy-tailed envelope — consistent with a near-Gaussian multi-carrier-like signal and not with a dominant single-carrier or strongly impulsive emission.

Higher-order complex statistics, to be read as a group: time_c20 0.01347046997398138 (near circular), time_c40 0.09711641818284988, time_c41 0.002406375017017126, time_c42 0.07561774551868439 — all small, indicating no strong second- or fourth-order non-circular/higher-order structure in this region.

Differential phase: time_differential_phase_std 1.7733128070831299 is close to the value expected for near-uniformly distributed phase increments, i.e. highly random adjacent-sample phase with no dominant tone; the reference notes this quantity is also affected by carrier frequency offset, sampling rate and low-amplitude noise, so it is supporting rather than decisive.

Autocorrelation structure: time_autocorrelation_peak_magnitude 0.06361924856901169 at time_autocorrelation_peak_lag_ratio 0.00048828125 (lag ≈ 2 samples at 4096-sample length), time_mean_autocorrelation_magnitude 0.015104892663657665, time_envelope_power_autocorrelation_peak 0.07615900039672852 — a weak peak that stands above a much lower mean level but in absolute terms is small, so it indicates at most a weak candidate repetition and, per the reference, cannot be claimed as cyclic-prefix or symbol-period detection.

Spectral shape: freq_normalized_mean_frequency 0.007523918990045786 and freq_normalized_median_frequency 0.010986328125 (near zero, baseband-centred with negligible residual offset), freq_normalized_peak_frequency -0.07177737355232239, freq_normalized_spectral_spread 0.276106595993042, freq_normalized_occupied_bandwidth_90 0.8547363877296448 (≈85% of the 1 MHz band occupied — wideband continuous occupancy), freq_normalized_spectral_skewness -0.011890054680407047 (near symmetric).

Spectral concentration measures, correlated and therefore not independent votes: freq_global_spectral_entropy 0.9881016612052917 (near maximal dispersion), freq_global_spectral_crest_factor 2.8789491653442383 (modest, no dominant narrowband peak), freq_global_spectral_flatness 0.8933407664299011 (close to flat). A flat, high-entropy, wideband spectrum fits a wideband multi-carrier emission, but the reference cautions that noise alone can also produce this pattern.
Absolute-scale features carry no class information and are recorded for completeness only: freq_log10_band_power 0.013727782294154167 and freq_psd_standard_deviation 4.5896751998952823e-07.

Bispectral block: freq_log_mean_bispectrum_magnitude -4.175708293914795, freq_log_max_bispectrum_magnitude -3.518707275390625, freq_log_bispectral_energy -3.8278067111968994, freq_normalized_bispectral_entropy 0.9472525119781494, freq_normalized_bispectrum_peak_frequency_1 -0.078125 with _2 0.109375, freq_mean_squared_bicoherence 0.03485684096813202, freq_max_squared_bicoherence 0.3275940716266632, freq_normalized_bicoherence_entropy 0.9597808122634888, freq_bicoherence_weighted_biphase_concentration 0.046521179378032684 — overall third-order coupling is weak (mean squared bicoherence 0.035) with one localized stronger point and little biphase concentration, i.e. no systematic quadratic phase coupling across the band.

STFT activity: time_frequency_stft_active_frame_ratio 1.0 with time_frequency_stft_energy_transition_ratio 0.0 and time_frequency_stft_frame_energy_cv 0.19684699177742004 — every frame within this 4.096 ms region is active and no activity state transitions occur, describing a continuous, non-bursty emission at the resolution of this short region.

STFT local spectral statistics: time_frequency_spectral_kurtosis_mean 1.8293901681900024 with std 0.0785260871052742, time_frequency_spectral_skewness_mean 0.00011754083971027285 with std 0.08827687054872513, time_frequency_spectral_crest_mean 5.8013224601745605 with std 1.0872254371643066, time_frequency_spectral_flatness_mean 0.5603544116020203 with std 0.03754185140132904, time_frequency_spectral_entropy_mean 0.9332602024078369 with std 0.008581703528761864 — locally symmetric, moderately flat spectra whose statistics barely vary over time, i.e. a stationary in-region emission.

Ridge and centroid tracking: time_frequency_normalized_stft_ridge_frequency_std 0.2509949505329132 with slope -0.19666706025600433, time_frequency_normalized_spectral_centroid_std 0.017905395478010178, time_frequency_normalized_spectral_spread_mean 0.27478548884391785 with std 0.008472904562950134, time_frequency_normalized_fsst_ridge_frequency_std 0.25002843141555786 with slope -0.10664472728967667 and curvature rms 0.1578206568956375 and ridge energy ratio 0.048859234899282455 and time-frequency entropy 0.9374758005142212, time_frequency_normalized_wsst_ridge_frequency_std 0.11730246990919113 with slope -0.025011148303747177 and bandwidth mean 0.12887540459632874 and std 0.017686229199171066 and ridge energy ratio 0.30957818031311035. The single-ridge statistics move around, which the reference attributes to ridge switching between components of a multi-carrier signal, whereas the power-weighted centroid is nearly constant (std 0.017905395478010178) and the low FSST ridge energy ratio 0.048859234899282455 shows energy is not concentrated in one ridge — together a wideband spread emission with no single dominant sweeping component.

Net reading of the feature block: it characterizes a continuous, stationary, wideband, near-Gaussian, low-higher-order-structure multi-carrier-like emission with no burst gaps, no dominant tone and no systematic quadratic coupling. It is compatible with an LTE downlink-like continuous wideband OFDM emission and does not contradict the LTE ensemble; it also does not separate LTE from DVB-T, which is the discrimination the periodicity stage was meant to supply and which is below threshold here.
conflicting_evidence: iq_member_3 region top1 is DVB-T 0.5340903997421265 against LTE 0.4632702171802521 — a 0.0708201825398744 margin, i.e. a near tie — and its windows flip LTE 0.7306716442108154 → DVB-T 0.8001691102981567, which is the sole member-level disagreement recorded by the risk gate.
risk_gate unanimous = false with reason member_region_top1_disagreement, so the ensemble mean is averaging over an actual member label conflict rather than over unanimous members.

The periodicity stage's prediction_label is DVB-T and its dvbt_2k_score 0.04958228021860123 exceeds lte_score 0.03416508436203003, but the margin 0.015417195856571198 is below the frozen reliability_margin 0.021475793793797496 and the correlations are at noise-like magnitudes, so this direction is not admissible evidence for DVB-T and does not outweigh the ensemble.

The feature block cannot discriminate between the two wideband multi-carrier candidates LTE and DVB-T: its spectral flatness, entropy, PAPR, near-Gaussian envelope kurtosis and weak autocorrelation peak are equally compatible with either, leaving the LTE call resting mainly on the two near-certain stable members rather than on independent signal-physics confirmation.

The weak in-band autocorrelation (time_autocorrelation_peak_magnitude 0.06361924856901169, time_envelope_power_autocorrelation_peak 0.07615900039672852) and the below-threshold periodicity stage mean no repetition or cyclic-prefix structure was independently confirmed, so the LTE recommendation is a model-dominant verdict rather than a structurally verified one.
limitations: Single 1 MHz / 4.096 ms observation region — a local short-time snapshot with no frame-level or synchronization structure, so the recommendation cannot speak for other regions or times.
Ensemble probabilities and correlations are model outputs, not calibrated probabilities or confidence estimates.
Window flips only indicate in-region non-stationarity; here the iq_member_3 flip is not taken as detection of any synchronization or frame structure.
iq_member_1/2/3 are same-type correlation models, so their agreement and disagreement are not calibrated independent evidence and one shared failure mode would move all three.
The periodicity gate returned reliable=false, so no periodicity-based corroboration or correction is available for the LTE call.

The 64 global features are statistical descriptors of one RMS-normalized, DC-removed region; several of them (spectral entropy, flatness, crest factor, and their time statistics; the four higher-order cumulants) are mutually correlated and have deliberately not been counted as independent confirmations, and none of them is a protocol or modulation label.
Feature values are sensitive to sampling rate, region length, SNR, amplitude normalization and receive gain, and this is a single extraction (extraction_count 1) with no cross-region replication.

This is a blind, non-operational experimental recommendation for an input already marked review_required with automatic_resolution unresolved, not a final decision; the fallback to abstention was not needed because the ensemble, the member pattern and the feature block are mutually consistent, but the medium confidence reflects the unverified periodicity stage and the one dissenting member.
